EV-01_answerable_from_existing_docs.reading: The answer usually already exists. The failure is in delivering it, not in having it.

EV-04_intents.reading: These four classes are a hard escalation rule rather than a threshold, because the label is a property of the class and not of how sure the classifier happens to be.

EV-06_expected_routing.ceiling_note: 62.2% is the labelled ceiling on first contact resolution. A system answering more than that is answering things it should not.

EV-08_ticket_length.reading: Every ticket is short. The longest is 276 characters, so any analysis that buckets at 500 characters finds an empty bucket and reports no variation.

interview_claims_tested.claim: Enterprise customers are resolved on first contact more often than standard ones.
interview_claims_tested.verdict: contradicted: the gap is 5.8 points in the opposite direction to the claim

interview_claims_tested.claim: Tickets written in non-fluent English are resolved less often today.
interview_claims_tested.figure: fluent 43.2% (n=380) vs non-fluent 45.8% (n=120); mean length 163 vs 145 chars
interview_claims_tested.verdict: not supported: the gap is 2.6 points, under 5.0

interview_claims_tested.claim: Longer, more complex tickets are harder to resolve on first contact.
interview_claims_tested.figure: longest quartile (>181 chars, n=115) 47.8% vs shortest quartile (<140, n=115) 35.7%
interview_claims_tested.verdict: contradicted: the gap is 12.1 points in the opposite direction to the claim

interview_claims_tested.claim: The client needs a chatbot because answers are missing.
interview_claims_tested.figure: 71.4% of tickets are answerable from the existing 29 articles, yet only 61.3% of those are resolved first time (against 0.0% of the rest)
interview_claims_tested.verdict: contradicted, and this is the central finding. Where the answer already exists, it still fails to reach the customer four times in ten. The constraint is delivery, not availability, so a chatbot that generates more answers addresses the wrong half.

interview_claims_tested.claim: Tickets that are not resolved first time come back.
interview_claims_tested.figure: not: 38.4% repeat (n=281); resolved first time: 0.0% repeat (n=219)
interview_claims_tested.verdict: supported, and it compounds the cost: every unresolved ticket is close to a second ticket as well as an escalation.
